text: The library was not a place of learning. It was a graveyard of drafts.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik stumbled through the doorway as it sealed behind them, the calcified key fused to his left hand scraping against the obsidian floor. Gray necrosis had climbed past his elbow now, spreading in delicate branching lines beneath his skin. Every heartbeat forced something thick and cold through the veins that remained. It no longer felt like blood. The sensation had settled into something stranger, as though ink itself had replaced whatever the City had already taken.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ahead of him, Ninsun slowed just enough to study the room before continuing. She no longer glanced toward corners or searched for hidden exits. Somewhere during their descent she had abandoned the hope that every chamber concealed another way out. Now she looked only for patterns—for repetitions in the stonework, for symbols carved where they did not belong, for the quiet logic that held the City together beneath all its contradictions.
speaker: Narrator

text: The chamber stretched beyond the reach of the torchlight. Black shelves rose in impossible rows, climbing into darkness so complete that they appeared to dissolve before reaching a ceiling. Upon them rested thousands of glass jars, each identical in size despite containing scenes that could not possibly fit inside. Some glowed with a pale, rhythmic light while others remained dark, yet even those seemed to pulse faintly whenever the City's distant breathing rolled through the floor beneath their feet.
speaker: Narrator

text: There was no smell of parchment or old leather, none of the familiar scents a library should have carried. The air tasted instead of dry stone, cold glass, and something faintly metallic that lingered at the back of Zik's tongue.
speaker: Narrator

text: It was only when he turned to speak—some half-formed instruction, the sort of thing he would once have tossed over his shoulder expecting Balag to answer before he had finished—that he realized how completely the silence had settled behind them.
